text: {"overall_winner":"A","qualities":[{"evidence":"“I am against driverless cars” and repeated defense of manual control","quality":"clear position","description":"It states a definite stance early and keeps that position consistently in view throughout the essay."},{"evidence":"workout analogy and train comparison","quality":"developed reasoning","description":"It explains its claims with extended analogies and cause-and-effect reasoning rather than just listing objections."},{"evidence":"“if every person in the United States were that way”","quality":"broader implications","description":"It pushes the argument beyond one driver to consider wider consequences if the same problem affected many people."},{"evidence":"“Who is laible for an accident…?” and “what if it doesn’t?”","quality":"argumentative inquiry","description":"It raises multiple pointed questions that deepen the debate over safety and liability."},{"evidence":"“Even with these negatives, I will awknowledge the positives”","quality":"balance and concession","description":"It explicitly acknowledges the other side before reaffirming its own position, which makes the argument feel more fair-minded."},{"evidence":"ending with “I stand my ground: manual control over a vehicle is better”","quality":"conclusive closure","description":"It closes with a firm restatement of the thesis that gives the essay a clearer sense of resolution."}]}
